neighbours.label: a family / home / household word naming the environment a person grew up in (raised in a … household, from a … family, an army brat); the same words as a building, a product line or a present-day family stay quiet
fire: He spent his childhood in a household where nobody ever raised their voice.
Growing up in a poor family taught her the value of every dollar.
The singer was brought up in a strict Catholic household outside Dublin.
Children raised in a bilingual home often switch languages mid-sentence.
Having come from a large family, he was used to sharing everything.
The novelist, a navy brat, moved eleven times before finishing high school.
She was the youngest child in a family of doctors and never doubted her path.
Kids who grow up in a single-parent home may take on chores early.
quiet: He spent his vacation in a hotel where nobody ever raised their voice.
The realtor showed them a two-storey home with a large garden.
This family of fonts includes bold, italic and condensed styles.
The retirement home on Elm Street is hiring two nurses.
Our family drove to the mountains for the long weekend.
The household appliances aisle is at the back of the store.
The novelist, a keen sailor, moved eleven times before finishing the book.
She spent her twenties in a laboratory studying fruit flies.
